html:
The University of Cape Town (UCT) was founded in 1829 as the South African College, a school for boys in the Cape Colony. It became a full university in 1918 and is the oldest university in South Africa.

Its main campus sits on the slopes of Table Mountain, on land left to the nation by Cecil Rhodes. The medical school's Groote Schuur Hospital was where Christiaan Barnard carried out the first human heart transplant in 1967.

Under apartheid the government restricted which students it could admit by race, and UCT protested as an "open university", though it still largely served white students. It became fully open in the 1980s and 1990s.

In 2015 students at UCT began the Rhodes Must Fall protest, which got Rhodes's statue removed from the campus and set off a wider debate about decolonising universities, across South Africa and as far as Oxford.
sum: The University of Cape Town (UCT) was founded in 1829 as the South African College, a school for boys in the Cape Colony. It became a full university in 1918 and is the oldest university in South Africa.
